reviews.one_line_contribution: It re-audits a specific published claim (ReMe's Qwen3-8B-with-memory beating memoryless Qwen3-14B) by making explicit two accounting choices that memory papers leave implicit — which cost is counted (prompt tokens vs generated tokens vs GPU-seconds vs wall-clock) and over how many future tasks N the write-path cost is amortized — and reports a break-even horizon N* with a CI plus the rank correlation between memory-system orderings across cost definitions and horizons.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Three verified papers jointly cover most of the mechanism. (1) 'Token Reduction Is Not Cost Reduction' (arXiv:2607.12161, verified via s2cli paper; 2026-07-13, S2) already establishes the exact epistemic move — that methods must be ranked by cost per *successful* task including cache behaviour, and that token counts reorder methods relative to real billed cost — for tool-heavy coding agents; the proposal's P3 is that paper's finding transplanted to memory systems. (2) 'Agent Memory: Characterization and System Implications' (arXiv:2606.06448, verified, 2026-06-04) already profiles write-path vs read-path cost across memory paradigms and reports that construction-heavy designs push most cost into construction — which is the causal story behind the proposal's predicted token-vs-GPU-second flip, and arguably behind P4 as well. (3) AMA-Bench (arXiv:2602.22769, verified, 41 citations) already folds amortized construction cost into its headline cost column. The residual delta is real but narrow: the horizon N as an explicit swept free parameter, a break-even N* with a bootstrap CI, and a cost-matched *larger memoryless backbone* attached to a named memory-vs-scale claim on task-execution benchmarks. I found no paper doing that combination, so novelty is not zero — but it is a recombination of three published moves against one sentence in one table, and the ancestor result (Dehghani et al., 'The Efficiency Misnomer', 2021) is correctly acknowledged as the template. The target claim itself is verified: s2cli returns arXiv:2512.10696 (ReMe, 2025-12-11, ACL, 55 citations) with the summary line 'Qwen3-8B equipped with ReMe outperforms larger, memoryless Qwen3-14B', so the claim being attacked genuinely exists and is being cited.
reviews.strongest_objection: The amortization model is never specified, and for the system under attack it is probably the wrong model. ReMe is a *dynamic, self-evolving* procedural memory: it keeps distilling, judging, refining and pruning as tasks arrive. If write-path cost is incurred per task at a steady rate rather than paid once as construction capital, then spreading it over N does not shrink it, N* is undefined, and the entire framework (P2's 'N* CI lower bound exceeds the source papers' evaluation sets') collapses into a category error. The proposal never states whether the store is built once and frozen or updated continually, never gives a per-task write-rate, and never says what it reports if the amortized curve never crosses. Relatedly, N* only exists if 8B+memory's *steady-state* (N to infinity, write cost fully amortized away) GPU-seconds per solved task is already below 14B memoryless — that limit is a fixed comparison of prefill-inflated 8B inference against 14B inference, decided before any horizon is swept — so P1 and P2 are largely arithmetic consequences of the read-path measurement, not discoveries, and a bootstrap CI on a quantity that may be infinite is not well posed. A second, independent objection: P3's ranking statistic is Kendall tau over three memory systems, which can only take values in {-1, -1/3, 1/3, 1}; 'tau at most 0.33' and the refutation threshold 'tau at least 0.8' are therefore nearly the same coarse event (0.8 is unreachable except at tau=1), and bootstrapping a three-item tau has essentially no power. The headline sensitivity result rests on a statistic with four possible values.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: (a) State the write policy explicitly and model it: build-once-then-freeze (capital cost, amortizable, N* meaningful) versus continual self-editing (per-task marginal write cost, in which case report the write-to-read cost ratio at steady state and drop N* for that system, or define N* against a fixed per-task write rate). Report both regimes; the contrast between them would be a more interesting finding than N* itself. (b) Pre-declare the behaviour when the amortized curves never cross — report N* as censored/infinite with the fraction of bootstrap replicates in which it is undefined, rather than a CI that presupposes existence. (c) Replace the three-system Kendall tau with a ranking statistic that has resolution: expand to at least six systems (k in {1,3,7} crossed with abstraction level gives nine points), or report the sign and magnitude of pairwise cost-per-solved-task gaps with CIs and count how many pairwise orderings flip. (d) Meter with vLLM prefix caching both on and off, and report it as a cost definition of its own: 2607.12161's central finding is that caching dominates realized cost, and a fixed injected memory block is exactly the case where prefix caching collapses read-path prefill — a GPU-second result measured with caching off would be dismissed as an artifact of the serving configuration. (e) Since the risk section already concedes that ReMe's headline is the +8.83 Avg@4 gain, either commit to also replicating that gain with seeds (which would make the paper a genuine replication of the primary claim) or drop the framing that a published result is being overturned.
reviews.missing_baseline: The larger backbone *with* the same memory (Qwen3-14B + ReMe-style store, and ideally 32B + store). Without it the design only asks 'does memory substitute for scale?' and never 'does memory compose with scale?' — so every N* is computed against a control that has been deliberately deprived of the treatment, and a reviewer will immediately ask whether the cost-optimal deployment is 14B+memory, which could dominate both arms under every cost definition and make the whole N* axis moot. This baseline is cheap relative to the stated budget and its omission is conspicuous. Secondary omissions a reviewer would also raise: prefix-caching-on metering as a cost definition (see above), and a quantized-8B-with-memory arm, since 'a bigger model is cheaper per solved task' is the same argument that 'a quantized model is cheaper per solved task', and the paper's own logic invites it.
reviews.preprint_collision: No verified collision. The proposal's own check is above average for this pipeline — four named queries, IDs attached, an explicit 'empty for the mechanism' report on Query D, and a stated budget failure — and I credit the honesty of reporting an empty search as empty. Two problems with it, though. First, it attributes Queries A and B to WebSearch, and one of its two central claims of prior-art distance rests on a paper I could not verify: it says 'Verification (s2cli paper): MemDelta arXiv:2606.29914 confirmed (2026-06-29, 2 citations)', but `s2cli.py paper 2606.29914` returned 'not found on S2 or HF' on two separate attempts, and a title/content search ('MemDelta write-path cost ablation protocol LongMemEval...') returned nothing resembling it. 'Compact-Memory LLM Agents' (arXiv:2609.04915) is likewise not found, though at 2026-09 it is days old and plausibly unindexed. A claimed s2cli verification that does not reproduce is a defect in the submission, not a neutral. VERIFIED (s2cli, S2+HF channel): 2512.10696 ReMe (S2; ACL; 55 citations; summary states the memory-scaling claim verbatim), 2602.22769 AMA-Bench (S2, 41 cit), 2606.06448 Agent Memory Characterization (HF), 2607.12161 Token Reduction Is Not Cost Reduction (S2, 2026-07-13), 2512.02543 In-Context Distillation with Self-Consistency Cascades (HF; ALFWorld 2.5x / AppWorld 2x cost reduction, so it is correctly identified as the matched-compute control), 2602.06025 BudgetMem (HF), 2608.04843 MemoryCPT (HF). COULD NOT VERIFY: 2606.29914 (MemDelta), 2609.04915 (Compact-Memory LLM Agents). My own searches, all answered by the s2cli channel (S2+HF; WebSearch is unavailable in this session and WebFetch is blocked, so channel (b) was not used): (1) 'amortized memory construction cost break-even horizon agent memory cost per solved task' --recent — returned MemoryCPT 2608.04843, Oracle Agent Memory 2607.13157, AgenticSTS 2607.02255, AutoMem 2607.01224, 2606.24775, 2606.06448; none reports a break-even horizon. (2) 'cost definition changes method ranking efficiency misnomer GPU-seconds versus tokens LLM agent evaluation' — returned Tokenomics 2601.14470, 'How Do AI Agents Spend Your Money' 2604.22750, 'LLM Inference Should Be Evaluated as Energy-to-Token Production' 2605.11733, 'Cheaply Evaluating Inference Efficiency Metrics' 2305.02440; cost-metric plurality is a live topic but none applies it to agent memory rankings. (3) closest named method, 'ReMe memory management kit procedural memory small model with memory outperforms larger model BFCL AppWorld' — returned ReMe 2512.10696 itself, plus Memp 2508.06433, 'Managing Procedural Memory in LLM Agents' 2606.23127, 'Agent Memory Distillation' 2608.07169 and 'Lightweight LLM Agent Memory with Small Language Models' 2604.07798 (the last three are small-model-memory papers that make adjacent claims without cost accounting — 2608.07169 in particular is a small-agent-plus-teacher-memory claim the proposal does not cite and probably should). (4) 'amortization horizon number of future tasks memory construction cost break-even ranking flips across cost metrics' --recent — nothing on horizons; closest were 2606.18144 (flash-endurance pricing, off-axis) and 2606.06448 again. (5) 'cost-matched control smaller model with retrieval memory versus larger model without memory equal compute agent benchmark replication seeds' --recent — returned EvoMemBench 2605.18421 (notable and uncited: reports that long-context baselines still outperform specialized memory methods), 'Memory Reward Inflation in Self-Improving LLM Agents' 2608.00017, LycheeMemory V2 2608.12990 ('reducing construction costs'); no cost-matched larger-backbone control for a memory-vs-scale claim. Conclusion: the specific package (horizon-indexed frontiers + N* + cost-matched larger backbone on a named memory-vs-scale claim) is not scooped, but its two nearest components are published and verified (2607.12161, 2606.06448), which is why novelty scores 5 rather than higher.
